verdicts.summary: A fetch that hangs records no failure until its 5-minute limit runs out, so the failure backoff never builds up. Every status refresh after the 15s cache TTL joins the stuck fiber and waits the full 5s.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The upstream host is blackholed: packets are dropped and nothing answers (for example a VPN-only host while the VPN is down), so ssh or https connect hangs for the OS or curl connect timeout, about 75-300s. 2) t=0: statusDetailsRemote forks the fetch. The waiter times out at 5s (1314-1316) and the cache stores success for 15s (1553). 3) t=15s and every 15s after: the cache misses. `failure` is undefined because tapError (1300) has not fired, so the gate at 1280 passes. The lookup finds the pending fiber (1283-1284) and joins it for another 5s. 4) Only when the fetch exits is count=1 / retryAt=+30s recorded. The next fetch hangs again. Before this change the fetch was killed at 5s, the failure was recorded right away, and cooldown grew 30s→60s→…→15min, so most status reads returned at once. Now about every status refresh (vcsRefreshStatus RPC, broadcaster ticks, the post-pull refreshGitStatus) costs 5s for as long as the host stays unreachable. Several such repos also hold the 4 global permits (1302), so healthy repos' fetches queue and show stale behind counts.
verdicts.consequence: Status refreshes stall 5s each, repeatedly and with no escalating backoff, while the remote is blackholed. Healthy repos' upstream refresh is delayed while the global slots are held.

verdicts.summary: The only real hazard here is the unbounded Fiber.await before the pull, which is finding 0. I also tried a key mismatch between the status fetch and the pull and could not build one: both resolve the realpath'd common dir through resolveGitCommonDir, and status matches the longest remote name first, which agrees with branch.<b>.remote for normal and slash-named remotes. The retry guard (same branch, same HEAD) also held.
verdicts.scenario: I tried four cases: the pull and the status fetch reaching gitCommonDir through different paths; remote names with slashes ('team/upstream'); a branch whose remote is '.'; and a lock failure after HEAD has moved. Keys match in the normal cases, and the guard at 2715-2721 blocks the retry once HEAD or the branch has moved. The remaining delay is finding 0.
